acceptance: The stable package exports a closed v1 data-classification level vocabulary and closed v1 lifecycle vocabularies with dataclass and datapolicy node kinds and declared required and optional fields, without framework, model-provider, or database coupling.

Deterministic node validation rejects any value outside a declared vocabulary with the stable error code DOMAIN_INVALID_ENUM_VALUE, and unknown node kinds and unknown attribute fields keep failing closed.

Deterministic node validation reports a datapolicy that declares bounded retention without an explicit deletion path as DOMAIN_LIFECYCLE_CONTRADICTION, while a policy that declares a deletion path is accepted.
Issue collection remains total and deterministic across repeated runs, node insertion orders, and JSON object key orders, under the documented phase order and sort key.
Domain validation does not mutate, reorder, or normalize its input, and well-formed Product Graph v1 canonical revision identity is unchanged by domain validation.
Focused classification and lifecycle tests plus the full repository format, lint, typecheck, and test suites pass on the exact candidate, and Ubuntu and Windows CI both pass.
Diffcipline exact-candidate proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments are recorded before guarded merge.

required: Stable @ineractive/product-graph v1 classification and lifecycle vocabularies, dataclass and datapolicy node kinds, enum-field validation, and the lifecycle contradiction rule, with focused deterministic tests.
Proof that out-of-vocabulary input fails closed with a stable error code and that canonical revision identity is unchanged for well-formed documents.
Exact-candidate Diffcipline proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments.
Exact-head Ubuntu and Windows repository CI plus post-merge fresh-main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Extend the already-qualified stable package with one bounded data-driven vocabulary and node-kind addition plus focused tests, instead of adding a package, promoting the prototype lab, or introducing a runtime dependency.

requirements: Classification and lifecycle validation composes on top of the SG-000020 node layer and the Product Graph v1 core contract and must never weaken or bypass either.
Deterministic validation must not depend on object iteration accidents, wall-clock time, randomness, network calls, or model inference.
Declaring a data class or a lifecycle policy must never be presented as legal or regulatory compliance, and no validator may claim compliance.

outcome: The stable @ineractive/product-graph domain layer defines a closed v1 data-classification vocabulary and closed v1 data-lifecycle vocabularies, adds deterministic dataclass and datapolicy node kinds with declared required and optional fields, rejects values outside a declared vocabulary with a stable error code, and reports a policy that declares bounded retention without a deletion path as a deterministic lifecycle contradiction.
rationale: IN-P02-S02-T02 requires data classification, lifecycle, privacy, locale, and external-effect semantics with deterministic validators. This Grain delivers the classification and lifecycle node slice first, because the governance relations and cross-node rules of the remaining IN-P02-S02-T02 slices need these node kinds and vocabularies to exist first.

risk.recovery: Revert the SG-000022 classification and lifecycle vocabularies, the dataclass and datapolicy node kinds, the enum-field validation, the lifecycle contradiction rule, the focused tests, the evidence record, and the current-frontier update; the SG-000019 through SG-000021 domain layer, the Product Graph v1 contracts, and ADR-0003 remain intact and no production state is mutated.

scope_in: Add the closed v1 data-classification level vocabulary and the closed v1 lifecycle vocabularies for retention, deletion, export, audit, and residency to the domain-semantics module of the stable @ineractive/product-graph package, taking the canonical DataClass list in docs/canonical/PRODUCT_GRAPH.md as authority and mapping the docs/canonical/RUNTIME_AND_SECURITY.md privacy list onto it.
Add the deterministic dataclass and datapolicy domain node kinds with declared required and optional attribute fields, leaving every existing node-kind contract unchanged.

Declare a data-driven enum field table so one node attribute can be constrained to a closed vocabulary, and report any value outside that vocabulary as the stable node-phase error code DOMAIN_INVALID_ENUM_VALUE.
Report a datapolicy that declares bounded retention without an explicit deletion path as the stable node-phase error code DOMAIN_LIFECYCLE_CONTRADICTION.

Add focused deterministic tests covering every newly declared vocabulary value, every declared enum field, out-of-vocabulary values, a missing classification level, the lifecycle contradiction, deterministic issue ordering, no input mutation, and unchanged canonical revision identity.
Advance specs/CURRENT.md to record SG-000021 canonical closure and SG-000022 as the active frontier Grain.
scope_out: No data-governance relations: no classified_as or governs relation, no cross-node classification or policy rules, and no change to the existing edge-kind vocabulary or endpoint compatibility.

No privacy semantics, no consent, purpose, visibility, redaction, minimization, locale/timezone, or external-effect semantics, and no Dataset, design-system, skill, exploration-branch, or release semantics.
No Change Intent, proposed graph delta, Question Gate, Assumption Ledger, graph views, compiler, database, Supabase migration, or remote side effect.
No node kind beyond dataclass and datapolicy, no change to the required or optional fields of existing kinds, and no relaxation of existing rejection behavior.
No new workspace package, no new runtime dependency, no lockfile change, and no change to Product Graph v1 public contract semantics or to canonical revision identity for well-formed documents.
title: IN-P02-S02-T02A Implement data classification and lifecycle node semantics
